project_name: Explicit Interaction-State Modeling for Binding-Affinity Change
domain: AI for Drug Discovery / biomolecular interaction modeling
core_question: How can local molecular interaction or binding-interface structure become an explicit computational object whose representation changes under local edits or mutations, so that the change can be used to predict binding-affinity effects?
excluded_or_rejected_framings: forcing the core problem into a sequential world-model framing solely because edits can be ordered
priority_questions: What should count as the explicit interaction state: residue/atom contacts, pair features, local geometry, energy-like terms, or a learned object?
Which real task best exposes the value of explicit local state change rather than global end-to-end encoding?
How much experimental affinity-change data exists, and what split/generalization settings are scientifically meaningful?
Do existing methods already explicitly update interface representations after mutations/edits, or only re-encode the full complex?
Where do structure-based affinity-change models fail under family/complex/OOD split?
